# The phases, step by step

`npm run heldout -- advance KEY` runs these in order and names the subagent each one needs. Read this when a step
needs a closer look, or when you run one by hand. `H="npm run heldout --"` (in Windows PowerShell,
`npm run heldout '--' …`).

| # | Phase | You do | Command / output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Fetch** | Pull the story's title, description and acceptance criteria, the screenshots they show and the Confluence pages they link (comments and other attachments are not requirement), into the folder of its AUT profile. A re-fetch detects requirement revisions | `$H fetch KEY [--aut <profile>]` → `1-requirement/` (+ `CHANGES.md`, `revisions/`) |
| 1b | **Contract** | `$H contract KEY --pack`, then **delegate** the building to the `heldout-contract-extractor` subagent. From the evidence pack alone it writes: each AC verbatim with cited lines; rules, endpoints, error cases, auth and test data; **gaps**, each either *mechanics* (HOW: left open, discovered in phase 3) or *oracle* (WHAT: found in the requirement, otherwise left open or assumed for the verdict to report); and a coverage ledger for every source line. Then delegate an **independent review** to the `heldout-contract-reviewer` subagent, in a fresh context. Send findings back to the builder and re-review until `$H contract KEY` is clean (after 3 rounds, what is still disputed becomes an open question). **Don't ask the user** the open oracle questions it lists: they go to the tests and the verdict | `2-contract/contract.json`, `2-contract/review.json` — [requirement-contract](requirement-contract.md) |
| 2 | **Write the tests** | **Delegate** to the `heldout-test-author` subagent ("Write the tests for KEY"). With no browser and from the reviewed contract alone, it runs `$H scaffold KEY`, lists the application's journeys (`$H journeys KEY`) and writes the Playwright TS tests: one user journey each, tagged with its `@AC-n`, one `@type` (what it truly proves) and a `// from` source, written in two passes: one test per criterion first, then round the test types per criterion for what the requirement implies; the steps call journeys, adding the missing ones to their domain's file (`journeys/fixtures/<domain>.ts`); every data precondition seeded; every expectation in the test (`expectResponse(…, '[REQ AC-n] …')`, `[REQ AC-n]` messages, `@req-constants`); guessed mechanics marked `// TODO(harden)`; lint clean (`--allow-unhardened`), and as its last command the draft marked finished (`lint KEY … --draft-finished`): `advance` freezes only a draft with that mark, so one whose author was cut off goes back to the test author. The open questions it returns are already in the tests (`// OPEN-QUESTION:`, `@needs-clarification`) and reach the verdict; nobody is asked | `3-tests/<key>.spec.ts`, `3-tests/test-data.json`, `journeys/fixtures/<domain>.ts` — [test-authoring](test-authoring.md), [journeys](journeys.md), [data-and-journeys](data-and-journeys.md) |
| 3 | **Freeze + harden** | **You** freeze the draft together with the contract's oracle (and a hash of each journey it uses): `$H integrity KEY --snapshot`. The draft stays as frozen in `3-tests/`; the hardener gets its own copy in `4-hardening/`, the tests that run. Then **delegate** to the `heldout-hardener` subagent ("Harden the tests for KEY"). It makes the mechanics work against the live AUT with the browser and API tiers, in the tests and the journeys they call, resolves the open mechanics gaps (`discovered-in-aut`, which changes no reviewed content), saves an accounts recipe when the story needs users, and proves stability with `$H run KEY --label harden --repeat-each 3 --workers 2`. Check `$H integrity KEY` yourself afterwards. When it reports an over-strict assertion implementation, **you** decide on `$H integrity KEY --amend` | `3-tests/freeze.json`, `4-hardening/` (the hardened tests, `hardening.md`, the probes it cites) — [hardening](hardening.md) |
| 4 | **Run** | **You** run the full suite. Preflight (lint, contract and review, journeys, 3-sample healthcheck) runs automatically; a down or **degraded** AUT aborts the run (`--allow-degraded` overrides) | `$H run KEY --label eval` → `5-run/NN-eval.json` |
| 5 | **Triage** | **Delegate** to the `heldout-triager` subagent ("Triage run NN-eval of KEY"). It auto-classifies, **reproduces each failure live** and records each decision with evidence; it never edits the tests or the journeys. Send the script defects it confirms to the `heldout-hardener` ("Repair these script defects for KEY: …"), re-run everything (`$H run KEY --label rerun`) and triage again (the triager uses `--carry-from auto`). At most 3 cycles in a row. The triager starts from the report's groups of failures that look alike and from the run's `all.chain.json` (in the scratch area); a failure on an assumed reading that is wrong under every reading is recorded with `--any-reading` | `6-triage/decisions.json`, the cited live reports in `6-triage/` — [triage](triage.md) |
| 6 | **Verdict** | Render the recommendation with traceability, reproduction and evidence | `$H verdict KEY` → `7-verdict/verdict.md`, `7-verdict/verdict.json` — [verdict-and-publish](verdict-and-publish.md) |
| 7 | **Publish** | Attach the verdict, post a summary comment, set a label. Nothing else. Part of the evaluation, with no confirmation; a project that wants a person to publish sets `jira.publish` to `"manual"`, and `advance` then leaves this step out | `$H publish KEY` |
| 8 | **Journey registry** | Record in `journeys/registry.yml` the journeys this story's passing tests used (this story as their proof, and what ran before each), and the stale marks. Journeys only failing tests used are left out. Preview, then apply; commit `registry.yml` with the journey files, `application-map/` and the story's output. After merging other people's work, `$H journeys --check` lints every journey and lists possible duplicates; a merge conflict in `registry.yml` is settled by `$H journeys --resolve` | `$H journeys KEY --harvest` → `--harvest --apply` → `journeys/registry.yml` — [journeys](journeys.md) |
| 9 | **Knowledge** | Keep the judged story's requirement for the next stories: its contract's rules and the gaps its owner answered become the application's required rules (assumed and open gaps don't), read by later hardeners and triagers after their freeze; what is left out is said | `$H map KEY --harvest` → `application-map/<profile>/app.yml` |

## When `advance` hardens by itself

When a draft leaves nothing to discover (every journey its tests call is proven in the registry as it is and holds no
`TODO(harden)`), `advance` does the hardening itself: it runs the tests twice, and when each one passes or fails on a
requirement assertion alone, it records the mechanics gaps as answered by those journeys, writes the hardening log and
goes on to the evaluation run. A guess left in a test (a locator built from a text the requirement gives) is settled
by that run: its test passed both times, on a line that acts on or expects what it locates. So is a journey that is
new with the story, when the new ones are fewer than the proven ones and every test that uses one passed both times;
a guess in it counts only on a statement of the journey itself that clicks, fills or waits for what it locates. A
guess in a branch, a path or field of an API call, a value a journey returns, a constant or a helper of the file all
go to the hardener, and so does anything else in that run (a locator that no longer matches, a failed precondition,
a flaky test).
